newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK November trade deficit seen widening.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK November trade deficit seen widening.

text.p: Britain's visible trade deficit with the rest of the world is likely to show a slight widening in November because figures already released show the non-EU trade gap widened that month, economists said.

The Reuters consensus forecast for trade figures due at 0930 GMT on Tuesday is for a deficit of around 770 million stg in November world trade in goods compared with an October shortfall of 454 million.
The non-EU trade deficit for December is forecast at 660 million stg compared with 639 million in November.
"In particular, we expect a rise in the underlying (excluding oil and erratics) deficit from October's low level," analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell wrote in their weekly look ahead.
"At the non-EU level, we look for a broadly unchanged deficit in December as a decline in the oil deficit is offset by a lower erratics surplus."
Michael Saunders of Salomon Brothers expects narrower deficits than the consensus, forecasting a world trade deficit of 600 million stg for November and a December non-EU shortfall of 500 million.
"Sterling's recent sharp rise probably will be reflected in weaker import prices which, in the short term, likely will outweigh any adverse effect on trade volumes of the rising pound," he said.

"A similar effect should cause the non-EU trade gap to shrink slightly in December, with the rise in sterling against the U.S. dollar and Japanese yen reflected in a further sharp drop in import prices."
Philip Uglow of Union Plc said that on a trend basis, the total trade gap appears to be narrowing.
"However, given our buoyant forecast for domestic demand and sterling's recent appreciation, we expect to see a widening over the coming year as export volumes fall and import volumes rise," he said.
He forecasts a November world trade deficit of 800 million stg and a non-EU December shortfall of 675 million.
